kept.title: Denial of Service via unbounded buffer growth
kept.description: The parser accumulates data into a string in memory without adequate size constraints, potentially leading to heap exhaustion.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a large multipart/form-data request with massive chunks of data
Send the request with an excessively large field value
Monitor the memory usage of the node process to confirm it grows linearly with the input
kept.impact: Remote attackers can crash the application process, leading to service disruption.

kept.title: Insecure temporary file handling in benchmark utilities
kept.description: The benchmark code in parted-multipart handles files in insecure directories with weak naming schemes, potentially leading to file manipulation.
steps_to_exploit: Access the server where benchmarks are running
Predict the generated filename because it uses simple Math.random() in a predictable way
Create a malicious file at the predicted location before the application writes to it
kept.impact: Arbitrary file overwriting or local privilege escalation if the benchmark is run with high privileges.

kept.title: Unsafe use of Buffer.allocUnsafe
kept.description: Allocation of uninitialized memory buffers in benchmarks may expose sensitive data from previous operations.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger the execution of multipart buffer creation code
Read the content of the buffer allocated via Buffer.allocUnsafe before it is overwritten
Inspect the uninitialized memory for leaks of secrets or internal data structures
kept.impact: Exposure of sensitive heap data previously resident in the process memory.

kept.title: Missing input validation in path processing
kept.description: The custom basename implementation fails to account for edge cases in various character encodings or OS path separators.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a filename containing unexpected path separators
Observe if the path traversal or normalization bypasses expected safety checks
kept.impact: Potential for path traversal vulnerabilities when processing user-supplied file names.

kept.title: Use of unsafe character encoding patterns
kept.description: The Decoder prototype uses a custom decoding loop which may be susceptible to state machine confusion or incorrect multi-byte sequence handling.
steps_to_exploit: Send a specially crafted string with mixed encoded/non-encoded characters
Verify if the decoder state machine behaves unexpectedly
Attempt to inject control characters into parsed fields
kept.impact: Parsing errors leading to logic flaws or unexpected application behavior.

kept.title: Prototype pollution via object header parsing
kept.description: Header parsing uses Object.create(null) but manual assignment and property manipulation may be vulnerable to proto-pollution if not carefully restricted.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a multipart part with a header name like __proto__
Observe if the object property modification affects the prototype chain
kept.impact: Severe logic flaws or application crash if internal object prototypes are corrupted.

kept.title: Predictable random number generation in benchmarks
kept.description: The use of Math.random() for naming temporary files in benchmark utility is cryptographically insecure.
steps_to_exploit: Examine the source code to identify the PRNG algorithm
Predict subsequent 'random' filenames generated by the system
Pre-create malicious files to block or hijack the benchmark execution
kept.impact: Facilitates attacks on file operations in the benchmark environment.

kept.title: Incomplete handling of CRLF sequences
kept.description: The header parser logic for folding headers and multi-line content can be bypassed with malformed line breaks.
steps_to_exploit: Send a multipart request with malicious folding sequences in headers
Attempt to split header values or bypass header filters
kept.impact: Security bypasses related to header-based filtering or parsing logic.

kept.title: Use of deprecated and vulnerable dependencies
kept.description: The project includes several dependencies (e.g., outdated multipart parsers in benchmarks) with known vulnerabilities.
steps_to_exploit: Analyze the dependency tree using tools like npm audit
Identify vulnerable versions of parsed multipart modules in the bench directory
kept.impact: Increased attack surface due to the inclusion of known-vulnerable code in the repository.

kept.title: Lack of rate limiting in benchmarks
kept.description: Benchmark scripts run in an infinite loop (10000 iterations) without any pause or external limits.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger the benchmark scripts on an exposed production-like environment
Exhaust CPU resources on the target machine
kept.impact: Resource exhaustion leading to potential DoS if benchmarks are inadvertently deployed.

kept.title: Improper error handling leads to process crashes
kept.description: Multiple locations emit 'error' events, but callers may not have listeners, causing unhandled 'error' events to crash the process.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger a parsing error in a way that the emitter propagates to a listener-less instance
Cause an unhandled exception process crash
kept.impact: Unstable service due to unhandled promise rejections or EventEmitter errors.

kept.title: Potential for path injection in file stream creation
kept.description: Filename is joined directly into a filesystem path without strict validation.
steps_to_exploit: Supply a filename containing path traversal sequences like ../../../
Observe if files are created outside of the target directory
kept.impact: Arbitrary file write to the filesystem, leading to code execution.

kept.title: Use of insecure 'binary' encoding
kept.description: Binary encoding is used for string conversion, which can cause data corruption or security bypasses in multi-byte sequences.
steps_to_exploit: Supply payloads that rely on multi-byte characters to bypass security filters
Verify if the binary conversion corrupts the payload in a way that impacts filter logic
kept.impact: Security filter bypass due to data corruption during conversion.

kept.title: Exposure of debug info in logs
kept.description: Various commented-out code blocks reveal that debug-level logs were used, which if re-enabled would log sensitive data.
steps_to_exploit: Re-enable debugging logs in benchmarks or library code
Monitor the output to collect sensitive data processed during requests
kept.impact: Leakage of potentially sensitive form data through system logs.

kept.title: Insecure temporary directory root
kept.description: Hardcoding the temp directory to /tmp on Unix or C:/Temp on Windows without validating environment permissions.
steps_to_exploit: Determine that the process writes to a predictable, global temporary directory
Race the file creation process to gain control of files
kept.impact: Filesystem security risks associated with shared temporary directories.
